tagline: Every book you own, in one private reader
brief: An offline-first, private ebook reader for every DRM-free format (EPUB, PDF, TXT, Markdown, HTML, FB2), for heavy readers and for researchers who annotate. It should feel calm, trustworthy and premium-dark, and stay clear of store-style reading apps and the open-book-on-orange cliché.
criteria: Success: ownable among reading apps, recognisable at 16 px, works in one colour, sits naturally in the app's dark Paperback Bands UI.

concepts.name: Bookmark p
concepts.idea: The p of Pages, its tail cut like a bookmark ribbon: your place, kept.
rationale: Says reading without the open-book cliché, and stays clear of orange open-book app icons
The ribbon echoes what the app protects: bookmarks, highlights and notes that are never lost
Built from one ring, one stem and one 45° cut; a heavier small-size cut keeps the notch at 16 px
Paper and press-orange on ink, taken straight from the app's design tokens

recommendation: Adopt the Bookmark p as the OpenPages mark: paper-white on ink in the app, ink on light surfaces, press-orange only on the ribbon.
